Implementation Plan Plan for #6784: deterministic template-twin resolution of conflicted `.claude/hooks/*` files (unblocks #6772) Planning ref: the planning context records `08c4132ec756bf6acc2c12a1602a19d441de0ff2` on `main`. The local checkout I read is at `739e2e90f7670b6c2b092746759aa9588a752791`, also on `main`. There is no integration-branch metadata, so there is no branch mismatch. Clarification answers: Q1 → A (a trusted `files_touched:` block in the issue body grants exactly four paths). Q2 → A (only regular files directly under `.claude/hooks/` qualify; each needs a cleanly merged regular-file `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/` twin and must not be listed in the divergence file). Scope-mode: Hold Scope Reuse-audit: extends review_conflict_prepare.sh deterministic manifest union-merge block Scope-mode justification: The unblock judge fixed the exact change, and clarify answers Q1/Q2 fixed the exact file set. The work follows the existing pattern in `scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh`: resolve a known conflict shape in the trusted host step before the resolver runs, then either commit the two-parent `[ai-merge-resolve]` merge or let the path drop out of the resolver's unmerged set. Wider coverage (commands, `settings.json`, nested paths) was turned down in Q2. Heal intake, `files_touched_scope_guard.py`, sandbox admission (`review_untrusted_workspace.py check-paths`) and workflow YAML stay unchanged. All edits fit the four granted paths. The only extra beyond the minimum is the integration-sync deferral. It costs under 10 LOC, and without it a hook-only conflict on an `orchestrator/project-*` branch would hit the existing "merge replay failed" error instead of the fingerprint-checked commit. Under §6, correctness ranks above speed. ## Automation / scheduling (§20.E) - No new script. This extends `scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh`. - Entry point: the existing `review_autofix.yml` step "Prepare merge-conflict resolver prompt and pre-snapshot". It already runs `bash "${SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_DIR}/review_conflict_prepare.sh"` on PR synchronize, dispatch, sweep and poller conflict dispatch. No workflow edit. - No supervisor. No DB work. No `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry, because nothing new is introduced. - The flag is defaulted inside the helper (`${CONFLICT_HOOK_TEMPLATE_RESOLVE_ENABLED:-false}`, §8). It is not exported from `review_autofix.yml`, which is outside the grant. Assumption: the prepare step passes job env through. As written, it cannot pick up the `vars.` repo variable, so an operator turns the flag on by setting job/step env in the workflow. Wiring the repo var into the workflow needs its own grant later. ## Files likely to change (exactly the granted `files_touched`) 1. `scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh`: the new hook template-twin block, plus OR-ing its defer flag into two existing gates. 2. `tests/test_conflict_manifest_union_contract.py`: regression tests. They are picked up automatically by `main()` and already run by `ci.yml`, `mark-stable.yml` and `test-and-mark-stable.yml`. 3. `changelog.d/6772-conflict-hook-template-resolve.md`: a new fragment that follows the existing `changelog.d/*.md` shape (CLAUDE.md §20). 4. `README.md`: one new row in the Variables table, directly after the `CONFLICT_MANIFEST_UNION_ENABLED` row (about line 149). ## Functions / modules to implement ### A. New block in `scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh` **Placement.** Immediately after the allowlist capture and print (after the `if [ "${_resolver_allowlist_count}" -gt 0 ]; then sed ... fi` at about line 200). It goes before the comment `# Deterministic resolution for the generated workspace manifest`. This keeps it outside the `_union_block()` extraction region that the existing tests slice: that region starts at `MANIFEST_UNION_PATH=`. **Sentinel and flags.** The block opens with the comment `# Deterministic resolution for conflicted .claude/hooks/ files from their template twin`. It initialises `_hook_tpl_resolved=false` and `_hook_tpl_defer_commit=false`. Both names are new; I checked them against the existing `_mu_*` and `_fp_*` names. **Gate.** - The block runs only when `[ "${CONFLICT_HOOK_TEMPLATE_RESOLVE_ENABLED:-false}" = "true" ]` and `_resolver_allowlist_count -gt 0`. - When the flag is off, it prints nothing and changes nothing. That is today's behaviour: the hook stays unmerged, and `review_conflict_resolve.sh` check-paths refuses with `sandbox_path_host_only`. **Divergence registry.** Read it once from the merged index's stage 0, not from the worktree: `git show ":.github/ai/claude_template_divergence.json"`. Parse it with `jq`, which the script already uses. If the file is unmerged or missing, `git show` fails, the JSON is invalid, or `.divergent` is not an object, log `Hook template-twin resolve: skipped reason=divergence_unreadable` and resolve nothing (fail closed). **Per-path loop.** For each line of `RESOLVER_ALLOWLIST_FILE` that matches `^\.claude/hooks/[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$` (directly under `hooks/`, no sub-directories, a safe name), all of these must hold. Otherwise log `skipped path=

reason=` and leave the path unmerged. 1. **Live hook.** `git ls-files -u -- "$p"` has stages `1 2 3` or `2 3` (a two-sided content conflict; delete/modify is excluded). Every listed mode is `100644` or `100755`. The worktree path is not a symlink (`[ ! -L "$p" ]`). Reason tokens: `stage_shape`, `live_not_regular`. 2. **Twin location.** The twin is `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/`. `git ls-files -u -- "$twin"` is empty. `git ls-files -s -- "$twin"` gives exactly one stage-0 line with mode `100644` or `100755`. The worktree twin is `[ -f ] && [ ! -L ]`. Reason tokens: `twin_unmerged`, `twin_missing`, `twin_not_regular`. 3. **Not divergent.** `jq -e --arg k "hooks/" '.divergent | has($k)'` is false. Reason token: `divergent`. 4. **Resolve.** Copy the twin's mode and blob SHA from the index: `git update-index --cacheinfo "${mode},${sha},${p}"`, which collapses stages 1–3 into stage 0. Then run `git checkout -- "$p"`, which writes the worktree bytes from the index with the twin's mode. 5. **Verify.** - `git ls-files -u -- "$p"` is empty. - `git ls-files -s -- "$p"` shows the twin's mode and SHA. - `cmp` of the worktree against `git cat-file blob "$sha"` succeeds. - On any mismatch, print `::error::Hook template-twin resolve: verification failed path=

` and `exit 1` (fail closed; nothing is committed). - On success, log `resolved path=

twin= mode=` and set `_hook_tpl_resolved=true`. The hook is never added to any model input. Once it reaches stage 0 it drops out of the later `git ls-files --unmerged` capture into `CONFLICTED_PATHS_FILE` (about line 970), out of the resolver prompt's `git diff --diff-filter=U` list (about line 493), and out of `review_conflict_resolve.sh` check-paths. **After the loop, when `_hook_tpl_resolved=true`:** - Recompute `RESOLVER_ALLOWLIST_FILE` and `_resolver_allowlist_count` the same way the manifest block does. Leave `RESOLVER_INITIAL_UNMERGED_PATHS_FILE` alone: it is classification-only and should still record the initial conflict. - If the count is above 0, fall through. The manifest block and the resolver handle the rest; a manifest-plus-hook-only case commits through the manifest block's existing early-commit tail. - If the count is 0 and `HEAD_REF` matches `orchestrator/project-*` (same `case` as the manifest block), set `_hook_tpl_defer_commit=true` and log that the commit is deferred until the integration fingerprint check runs. - If the count is 0 otherwise, commit with a copy of the manifest early-commit tail: - `git rm -r --cached --ignore-unmatch -- node_modules` - the consumer-only `IS_WORKFLOW_SOURCE_REPO` reset/checkout of `prompts`, `.github/scripts`, etc. - `git commit -m "[ai-merge-resolve] resolve merge conflicts"` - stash restore, `rm -rf "${RESOLVE_STASH}"`, `rm -f "${_merge_stderr_file}"` - `echo "CONFLICT_RESOLVED=true" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"`, then `exit 0` `MERGE_CONFLICT` is not cleared, so the merged head is still re-reviewed. The tail is duplicated on purpose: refactoring it into a shared function would change the `_union_block` text that `test_prepare_early_commit_branch_contract` pins. ### B. Two one-line gate extensions further down the same script - The empty-allowlist check (about line 418): add `&& [ "${_hook_tpl_defer_commit}" != "true" ]`. - The deferred commit block (about line 728): change the condition to `if [ "${_mu_defer_commit}" = "true" ] || [ "${_hook_tpl_defer_commit}" = "true" ]; then`. Add a `Hook template-twin resolve:` log line inside it when the hook flag is set. The existing manifest-worded `::error::` and success strings stay unchanged, because other tests match them. ## Data structures affected - No persisted state or new files. - The merge index changes (a stage 0 entry replaces stages 1–3 for each eligible hook). - `${RUNTIME_DIR}/resolver_unmerged_allowlist.txt` is recomputed. - `GITHUB_ENV` gets `CONFLICT_RESOLVED=true` only on the hook-only commit path. ## API / interface changes - New env var `CONFLICT_HOOK_TEMPLATE_RESOLVE_ENABLED`, default `false`, defaulted inside the helper. - New human-readable log lines `Hook template-twin resolve: resolved|skipped path=... reason=...`. These are deliberately not registered as a stable log prefix, because `agents.md` is outside the grant. - No change to the workflow inputs or outputs, check-paths, the sandbox policy, or the resolver. Data flow: 1. Merge replay, then allowlist capture. 2. With the flag on, each eligible `.claude/hooks/` is replaced by its twin's index blob and mode. 3. The allowlist is recomputed. 4. Then one of: - count 0 on a non-integration branch: `[ai-merge-resolve]` commit, `CONFLICT_RESOLVED=true`, exit 0; - count 0 on an integration-sync branch: defer, then the existing fingerprint check and the deferred commit block; - coun
